C2.missing_piece: No known low-loss path carries usable power around the planet: the Earth-ionosphere cavity is a leaky resonator (Q about 5), so the transmitter would have to resupply its losses continuously.

requirements.statement: A guided surface wave (Zenneck/Norton type) must carry kilowatts over 10+ km with most of the power arriving
requirements.feasibility_basis: Surface-wave launching is demonstrated at lab scale only; field strength still falls with distance and ground losses dominate.
requirements.web_query: Zenneck surface wave wireless power transmission experiment

requirements.statement: Beamed power (microwave or laser) must deliver useful power over kilometres at high efficiency
requirements.feasibility_basis: Real kilometre-scale demos exist (DARPA POWER, NTT/MHI 2025) but end-to-end efficiency is still low.
requirements.web_query: power beaming record distance efficiency 2025 laser microwave

requirements.statement: The Earth-ionosphere cavity would need a quality factor in the thousands instead of about 5
requirements.feasibility_basis: Measured Schumann-resonance Q is 4-6, set by the conductivity of the lower ionosphere; no engineering lever changes it.
requirements.web_query: Schumann resonance quality factor measurement ionosphere losses

C2.missing_piece: The 97% figure has never been reproduced; measured disc turbines reach roughly 40%, mostly because of nozzle, exhaust and end-wall losses.

requirements.statement: Nozzle-to-rotor losses must fall below a few percent (flow entering the gaps at near rotor speed)
requirements.feasibility_basis: CFD studies keep finding the nozzle and inlet as the main loss; better designs gain points, not tens of points.
requirements.web_query: Tesla turbine nozzle design loss CFD efficiency improvement

requirements.statement: Disc gaps must stay at about twice the boundary-layer thickness at high speed, with flat, rigid discs
requirements.feasibility_basis: Micro-fabricated and additive-manufactured rotors make tight gaps possible at small sizes.
requirements.web_query: Tesla turbine disc spacing boundary layer additive manufacturing study

requirements.statement: Exhaust kinetic energy must be recovered instead of dumped
requirements.feasibility_basis: Diffusers help in bladed machines; little published work for disc turbines.
requirements.web_query: Tesla turbine exhaust diffuser energy recovery

C3.missing_piece: At today's measured efficiency a disc turbine would burn far more fuel than a bladed one at power-plant scale; its plausible niche is small, dirty or two-phase flows.

requirements.statement: Disc turbines must win a niche where blades fail: small organic-Rankine or waste-heat units
requirements.target: cost per kW below bladed micro-turbines under 50 kW
requirements.feasibility_basis: Several groups test Tesla expanders for ORC and waste heat; low cost and tolerance of wet vapour are real advantages.
requirements.web_query: Tesla turbine organic Rankine cycle waste heat expander 2025

requirements.statement: Efficiency at multi-MW scale must approach 85-90% to compete with bladed steam turbines
requirements.feasibility_basis: Depends on the 97% claim above being solved; no evidence of a path today.
requirements.web_query: large scale Tesla turbine megawatt efficiency
